recent_articles.title: Twisha Sharma’s husband sent to 7-day police remand; AIIMS Delhi forms panel for second autopsy - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samarth Singh**, husband of actor-model Twisha Sharma, was sent to seven days of police custody in Bhopal following his arrest for dowry death and harassment. **AIIMS Delhi** formed a four-member panel to perform a second autopsy on Sharma's body after the Madhya Pradesh High Court ordered it.  The probe team is investigating Mr. Singh's alleged role in Sharma's death, including questioning him and his mother, **Giribala Singh**, who was also named as an accused. The family has demanded a CBI investigation into the case, alleging police misconduct and influence from the accused family.

recent_articles.title: Twisha Sharma: Rival claims of murder and suicide set off media frenzy after Indian bride dies
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A dowry death case in India has sparked a media frenzy after the death of 33-year-old model and actor Twisha Sharma.  **Twisha's** parents allege she was tortured by her husband, **Samarth Singh**, and his mother, retired judge **Giribala Singh**, over dowry demands and that she was murdered. The police have lodged a case against the Singhs and are investigating whether her death was murder or suicide. **Giribala Singh** denies the allegations, claiming **Twisha** had mental health issues and committed suicide.  The case has drawn attention to the issue of dowry deaths in India, where thousands of women are murdered annually for bringing insufficient dowries.

recent_articles.title: Twisha Sharma death: Madhya Pradesh government proposes to transfer case to CBI - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Madhya Pradesh** government proposed transferring the dowry death case of Twisha Sharma to the **CBI**. The notification, issued by Home Department Secretary Krishnaveni Desavatu, cites the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act for extending investigative powers to the state.  The case, registered at Katara Hills Police Station, involves allegations of harassment and dowry-related deaths against her husband Samarth Singh and mother-in-law Giribala Singh.

recent_articles.title: Sedition trials can go on if accused is willing: Supreme Court - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** has lifted a four-year hold on sedition trials, allowing courts to proceed with cases where the accused do not object. The court clarified that if an accused consents to continued proceedings under Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), courts can decide matters on merits. This decision follows an interim order in 2022, during which the court had requested the government to reconsider the colonial-era provision.  The **Supreme Court** directed the Madhya Pradesh High Court to hear the petitioner's appeal and related cases.

recent_articles.title: Supreme Court declines to interfere with forest clearances for Adani’s Madhya Pradesh coal block project - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** declined to intervene in environmental clearances granted to the Adani Group's coal block project in Madhya Pradesh. The court noted a delay in challenging the approvals and observed that the National Green Tribunal (NGT) had relied on a 2025 ruling regarding limitation periods for challenges.  While the petitioner argued for judicial review of the clearances due to environmental concerns, the **Adani Group** urged dismissal of the plea. The court suggested Mr. Dubey pursue other legal remedies and granted him liberty to do so.

recent_articles.title: After High Court verdict, Hindu petitioners seek free entry for devotees at Bhojshala in Madhya Pradesh - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Hindu** petitioners have filed applications with the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** and the **Union Culture Ministry**, demanding free entry to the Bhojshala complex and the removal of "unauthorised Islamic symbols". They also requested that idols of Lord Hanuman and other Hindu deities be retrieved through a scientific excavation. The **Madhya Pradesh High Court** had declared the site a Vagdevi temple on May 15, quashing an earlier order allowing Muslims to offer namaz there.

recent_articles.title: Hindu groups perform puja at Bhojshala amid security; ASI issues directions to implement High Court order - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Hindu Front for Justice**, **Bhoj Utsav Samiti**, and local residents performed Aarti at the Bhojshala complex in Madhya Pradesh's Dhar on Saturday, May 16, 2026. The **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** acknowledged the High Court's verdict declaring the site a Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Saraswati and a Sanskrit learning center.  The ASI issued an order permitting unrestricted access for the Hindu community while ensuring monument conservation under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act, 1958. Muslim representatives have stated they will challenge the decision in the Supreme Court.

recent_articles.title: Bhojshala Case: What did the High Court decide? - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Madhya Pradesh High Court** ruled that the **Bhojshala-Kamal Maula** site is a Hindu temple, granting full worship rights. The verdict has sparked reactions from both sides and may now be appealed to the Supreme Court.

recent_articles.title: Sebi approves IPO plans of Neolite Lightings, Aspri Spirits and SS Retail - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Neolite ZKW Lightings**, a manufacturer of automotive lighting products, plans to raise Rs 600 crore through a combination of fresh issue and offer-for-sale. The IPO will be used for setting up a greenfield manufacturing facility in Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu, expanding existing operations, and repaying borrowings. **Neolite ZKW Lightings** has a significant market share in India's commercial vehicle lighting segment and serves over 40 OEM customers. Meanwhile, **Aspri Spirits**, an importer and distributor of international wine and spirits, received Sebi approval for its public issue with a proposed IPO of up to Rs 140 crore.  SS Retail, another company seeking regulatory clearance, plans to raise Rs 500 crore through its IPO, which will be used for expansion and growth.

recent_articles.title: Death toll in explosion at firecracker factory in M.P.'s Dewas rises to five - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Five workers have died after an explosion at a firecracker factory in Madhya Pradesh's Dewas district, with 23 others hospitalized. **Anil Malviya**, the licensed owner of the factory, has been arrested under the National Security Act (NSA) and his license suspended.  **Chief Minister Mohan Yadav** visited the hospital where the injured are being treated, promising a thorough investigation into the incident. The state government is also conducting a magisterial inquiry and has ordered an investigation by officials from the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organization (PESO), the State Pollution Control Board, and the Forensic Science Laboratory.

recent_articles.title: Indian pharma fuels Africa's 'zombie drug' and opioid crisis despite crackdown - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Indian pharmaceutical companies are exporting high-strength tapentadol tablets to west Africa despite a crackdown on illegal drug trade. The pills, which are often sold as tramadol and are much stronger than approved doses, are fueling a deadly opioid epidemic in the region.  The pills are being added to "zombie drugs" like kush, leading to increased addiction and health problems, including deaths from overdoses.  While India claims it has banned exports of tapentadol mixed with other drugs, shipments continue despite warnings from government officials in Nigeria, Sierra Leone, and Ghana. The Indian Drug Manufacturers’ Association defends the trade, stating that manufacturers are not responsible for what happens after their products leave their facilities. Experts warn that the lack of regulation and enforcement in Africa allows unscrupulous companies to exploit the market, leading to widespread misuse of the drug.

recent_articles.title: Blaze erupts after explosion at firecracker factory in M.P.'s Dewas; casualties feared - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A fire and explosion at an alleged illegal firecracker factory in Dewas district, Madhya Pradesh, resulted in multiple casualties. **Police** and **administration** personnel launched rescue operations after the incident, which occurred in Tonk Kalan area.  Local residents reported the factory was producing illegal fireworks.

recent_articles.title: Three held; security beefed up in Bhopal as Muslim community protests assault on man over ‘love jihad’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Three** men were arrested in **Bhopal**, **Madhya Pradesh**, following a protest by members of the Muslim community who demonstrated against an assault on a man by **Bajrang Dal** activists. The incident occurred after several videos of the assault, which allegedly involved derogatory language and insults to Islam, went viral online.  The Muslim community demanded that the accused be arrested within 24 hours.  **Ayush Gupta**, Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), Bhopal zone 1, confirmed searches for more suspects and stated that adequate security has been implemented in sensitive areas. **Bittu Sharma**, Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP), Jahangirabad, reported increased police presence in these locations to maintain peace. The incident followed a previous attack on Arif Khan, a 27-year-old man from the Muslim community, by right-wing activists who accused him of "love jihad."

recent_articles.title: SC asks Centre to consider States’ pleas for funds for CCTVs in police stations - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** urged the **Union government** to fully implement the Assistance to States and Union Territories for Modernisation of Police (ASUMP) scheme, which provides funds for installing CCTV cameras in police stations and a centralized monitoring dashboard. The court expressed concerns over non-functional CCTV cameras in Udaipur police stations and directed the Centre to consider requests from states for funding.  The ASUMP scheme has been extended until September 30, 2026, with most states initiating steps towards compliance. However, Jharkhand was criticized for not installing any CCTV cameras, despite receiving funds under the scheme. The court also cautioned against releasing funds without due diligence to prevent misappropriation.

recent_articles.title: PM austerity appeal: State leaders take steps to limit their fuel use - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Home Minister Amit Shah**, and several other state chief ministers have implemented measures to reduce fuel consumption in response to the West Asia crisis.  These include reducing convoy sizes, promoting electric vehicles, and encouraging public transport use. **Yogi Adityanath**, **Rekha Gupta**, **Mohan Yadav**, and others have also taken steps to promote sustainability within their respective states.  **Devendra Fadnavis**, **Harsh Sanghavi**, and **Acharya Devvrat** have implemented similar measures in Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Bihar respectively.

recent_articles.title: Four cheetah cubs die at Kuno in suspected leopard attack - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Four** cheetah cubs, born in April and the first to be born in the open forest since India's reintroduction program began in 2022, were found dead on Tuesday (May 12, 2026) in **Kuno National Park**, Madhya Pradesh.  The carcasses of the one-month-old cubs were partially eaten and marks of a leopard attack were found during post-mortem examinations. The mother cheetah is safe and healthy, according to officials. A thorough investigation is underway into the incident, which highlights the challenges of adapting cheetahs to their natural habitat.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Two cheetahs released into wild in Kuno; CM Yadav says M.P. now recognised as ‘Cheetah State’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav** released two cheetahs from Botswana into an open forest in Kuno National Park, marking another successful chapter of the **Project Cheetah**.  The reintroduction program aims to restore the endangered species and prepare them for free roaming. This is the third international phase of the project, following previous arrivals from Namibia and South Africa. The release follows a quarantine period and experts believe cheetahs from Botswana will contribute to a healthy and sustainable population in Kuno.

recent_articles.title: Bengaluru fire accident: One killed, four others critical in Nagarbhavi hotel blaze - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A fire broke out at a hotel in Malagala, near Nagarabhavi, India, on Friday night, resulting in the death of **Raj Kumar**, a 40-year-old hotel employee.  **Four colleagues** sustained severe burns and are currently hospitalized in critical condition. The fire is suspected to have been caused by a short circuit, spreading rapidly through the staff quarters where five workers were sleeping. Firefighters rescued all five workers but **Kumar** succumbed to his injuries during treatment.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal Cabinet 2026: From Dilip Ghosh to Agnimitra Paul, Ministers who were sworn in along with Suvendu Adhikari - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, newly sworn in as the Chief Minister of West Bengal, inducted five new ministers into his cabinet on Saturday. The swearing-in ceremony was attended by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Ministers Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, J. P. Nadda, and Dharmendra Pradhan**, among other BJP leaders.  **Dilip Ghosh**, a senior BJP leader who secured victory in the Kharagpur seat, **Agnimitra Paul**, a fashion designer-turned-legislator who won Asansol Dakshin, **Ashok Kirtania**, a BJP stalwart who gained victory in Bangaon Uttar, and **Kshudiram Tudu**, a former school teacher from Ranibandh (ST) constituency, were among the newly appointed ministers.  **Nisith Pramanik**, a key face of BJP from North Bengal, was also inducted into the cabinet.

recent_articles.title: IPO Calendar: 2 issues to keep investors busy but mainboard activity remains muted - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **RFBL Flexi Pack**, a Gujarat-based company that manufactures and trades printed multilayer flexible packaging materials, is raising Rs 35.33 crore through an IPO of 70.65 lakh shares. The company plans to use the proceeds for capital expenditure, working capital needs, and general corporate purposes.  **Goldline Pharmaceutical**, another company seeking to raise Rs 11.61 crore through a fresh issue of 27 lakh shares, operates an asset-light pharmaceutical marketing business selling medicines under its "Goldline" brand across various segments. The company plans to use most of the IPO proceeds toward repayment of borrowings.

recent_articles.title: Jabalpur cruise boat tragedy: Nightmare on the Narmada - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: On April 30th, **Madhya Pradesh** experienced a heat wave with temperatures exceeding 40 degrees Celsius.  As the weather cooled, people flocked to the Bargi dam reservoir on the Narmada river for boat rides and cruises operated by the **MPSTDC**. This popular destination has been a draw for locals and tourists for nearly three decades.

recent_articles.title: Census enumerators ID can be verified through QR code - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lalit Jain**, Director of Census Operations (DCO), **Haryana**, has introduced QR code-enabled identity cards for enumerators to address concerns about authenticity.  Jain explained that residents can verify the legitimacy of enumerators by scanning the codes on their ID cards. The first phase of the digital census, which began on April 1, aims to cover over 30 lakh households across India. Residents are legally obligated to answer Census-related questions, and while there have been no cases of FIRs for non-response, local authorities will be involved in encouraging participation.  The second phase of the census, focusing on caste enumeration, is scheduled for February 2027.

recent_articles.title: Congress blocks Agra-Mumbai highway in Indore over farmers’ issues - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** workers blocked the Agra-Mumbai National Highway in Indore, Madhya Pradesh on Thursday as part of a state-wide protest demanding attention to farmers' issues. **Vikrant Bhuria**, national president of the Adivasi Congress, accused the BJP government of neglecting farmer concerns and failing to guarantee minimum support prices (MSP). He also alleged irregularities within the soybean 'Bhavantar Yojana' and claimed that market yards were dominated by corporations.  The protest is expected to continue in phases.

recent_articles.title: Gurugram gated societies not letting in enumerators; FIRs recommended against enumerators obstructing Census work - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Haryana** administration has recommended an FIR against two government school staff for alleged negligence in Census-related work and obstruction of duties.  **Gurugram Municipal Corporation Joint Commissioner Punit Kumar** stated that enumerators have been denied entry into several highrise apartment buildings, prompting him to write to RWAs to ensure their access. **Registrar General of India Mritunjay Kumar Narayan** flagged off awareness vans across Delhi for the ongoing Census 2027 public outreach campaign.  The first phase of the Census began on April 1 and will conclude by September 30, involving around 30 lakh enumerators.

recent_articles.title: In a first, world’s smallest wild cat snapped with kitten in Faridabad; confirms breeding outside protected areas, say researchers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Researchers**, including wildlife photographer Yatin Verma, have documented the first confirmed breeding of a rusty-spotted cat in the Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR) and Haryana.  The discovery was made during routine field surveys conducted since August 2022. The adult cat and its kitten were observed perched on a False Ashoka tree in Kot village, confirming active reproduction outside protected areas. This finding highlights the importance of the Aravalis mountain system for wildlife conservation, including the rusty-spotted cat, which is listed as 'Near Threatened' on the IUCN Red List.  The research paper documenting this discovery was published in Zoo’s Print.

recent_articles.title: Rise in cybercrime but overall crime rate dropped in 2024, says latest NCRB report - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB)** reported a 6% decline in overall crime in India for 2024, but cybercrime cases surged by over 17%.  **NCRB** data revealed that fraud constituted the majority of cybercrime cases, followed by sexual exploitation and extortion. The report also highlighted a rise in crimes against the state, with **The Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act** being the most frequently cited law. Suicide rates increased significantly in 2024, particularly among agricultural workers, unemployed individuals, daily wage laborers, and students.

recent_articles.title: Cabinet panel clears Railway Ministry’s three multitracking projects in six States - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs**, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved three multitracking projects for the **Railway Ministry** with a total cost of ₹23,437 crore. These projects will increase the existing railway network by about 901 km in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. The projects are expected to be completed by 2030-31 and will enhance connectivity to approximately 4,161 villages, improve rail connectivity to several tourist destinations, and provide seamless connectivity for people, goods, and services.

recent_articles.title: Put petty politics aside, says Rahul Gandhi, as he backs Mamata Banerjee - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, criticized the **BJP's** victory in the West Bengal and Assam Assembly elections as a "theft" of the popular mandate, alleging it marks a step towards destroying Indian democracy. He expressed support for the Trinamool Congress (TMC) and cautioned against political schadenfreude over the party's defeat.  Gandhi urged political parties to prioritize India above partisan considerations.

recent_articles.title: Put petty politics aside, says Rahul Gandhi, as he backs Mamata Banerjee - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, criticized the **BJP's** victory in the West Bengal and Assam Assembly elections as a "theft" of the popular mandate, alleging it was part of the party's attempt to destroy Indian democracy.  He expressed support for the Trinamool Congress (TMC) and urged political parties to prioritize national interests over partisan concerns. **Gandhi** also noted that this is not an isolated incident, referencing previous instances of electoral manipulation by the **BJP**.

recent_articles.title: Jabalpur cruise boat tragedy: Death toll rises to 11; search ops. on to trace two missing passengers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Two** more bodies have been recovered from the Bargi dam reservoir in Madhya Pradesh, bringing the death toll to 11 in the Jabalpur cruise boat tragedy. **Raghvendra Singh**, the Collector of the district, confirmed that two children were among the latest victims found.  The search for four missing passengers continues with over 200 rescuers involved, including divers and disaster response teams. The investigation is ongoing, with authorities investigating potential negligence by the crew and a ban on similar vessels in the state.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Around 82 lakh households have opted for self enumeration as field visits begin in 5 states - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Union government** announced that over 82 lakh households have utilized the self-enumeration facility during the initial Houselisting and Housing Operations (HLO) phase of Census 2027. The exercise, which commenced on May 1st in several states including Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Chandigarh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Rajasthan, aims to collect data about household facilities and demographics.  The HLO will continue until May 30th, with trained enumerators visiting each house for verification.

recent_articles.title: 15 labourers die as van overturns in Madhya Pradesh’s Dhar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: At least 15 laborers, many of them women, died and over 30 were injured in a road accident on the Indore-Ahmedabad highway in Madhya Pradesh's Dhar district.  The **police** said the speeding van carrying about 46 labourers overturned and collided with an SUV.  **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** expressed condolences and announced financial assistance for the victims, while **Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav** directed officials to oversee medical arrangements and provide financial aid.
